newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan shipping shares weak after US sanctions news.
newsitem.headline: Japan shipping shares weak after US sanctions news.

text.p: Shares in Japan's sea transport sector sank on Thursday morning, as sentiment was dampened by Wednesday's news the U.S. Maritime Commission would impose $100,000 port surcharges on Japanese vessels calling at U.S. ports, brokers said.
Share turnover, however, was relatively small.
The commission announced that the surcharge would take effect on April 14, in response to what it termed "unfavourable restrictive practices" at Japanese ports.

The commission said the surcharge will be imposed each time a vessel owned or operated by Kawasaki Kisen Kaisha Ltd, Mitsui O.S.K. Lines Ltd and Nippon Yusen KK enters a U.S. port from abroad, but not from another U.S. port.

At midday, Kawasaki Kisen dropped nine yen to 247 yen in a turnover of 168,000. Mitsui O.S.K. also fell seven yen to 248 yen in a turnover of 314,000. Nippon Yusen was unchanged at 483 yen in a turnover of 176,000.

The commission claimed that the Japan Harbour Transportation Association (JHTA), an association of Japanese waterfront employees, had put in place costly and restrictive practices that discriminate against foreign vessels.
